title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 13
description: Ten questions on Romans 13: subjection to the authorities, paying what you owe, love as the fulfillment of the law, and the armor of light.

questions.text: To what should every soul be in subjection?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1 says to let every soul be in subjection to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God.

questions.text: What does the one who resists the authority withstand?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:2 says that he who resists the authority withstands the ordinance of God, and those who withstand will receive judgment to themselves.

questions.text: Rulers are not a terror to the good work, but to what?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:3 says rulers are not a terror to the good work, but to the evil, and that doing good brings praise from the authority.

questions.text: Why should a person be afraid if he does what is evil?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:4 says the ruler is a servant of God and does not bear the sword in vain, being an avenger for wrath to him who does evil.

answers.text: Because the assembly will shut him out
Because the ruler doesn't bear the sword in vain
Because the land will not yield its fruit
Because his name will be forgotten

questions.text: Besides because of the wrath, for what reason should they be in subjection?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:5 says they need to be in subjection not only because of the wrath, but also for conscience' sake.

answers.text: For the sake of peace with the Gentiles
For the sake of the temple service

questions.text: What four things does the text tell them to give to everyone they owe?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:7 says to give everyone what you owe: taxes, customs, respect and honor.

questions.text: What is the one thing the text says they should owe?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:8 says to owe no one anything, except to love one another, for he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

answers.text: To give thanks at all times

questions.text: In which saying are the commandments all summed up?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:9 says the commandments and whatever other commandments there are, are all summed up in the saying, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

answers.text: “You shall not covet your neighbor's house.”
“You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
“Honor the authorities that are set over you.”
“Be holy, for the Lord your God is holy.”

questions.text: What are they to put on when they throw off the deeds of darkness?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:12 says the night is far gone and the day is near, so they should throw off the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

questions.text: Whom are they told to put on, making no provision for the flesh?
questions.explanation: Romans 13:14 says to put on the Lord Jesus Christ and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.
